BH-VIB-K16-FLUX-001 — MATHEMATICAL_INCONSISTENCY (high; established)

  • Source claim: Paper6B p9:cor:k16-timewidth-retired, lines 510–518. On a C^1 curvature branch, the source says χ_+ dot R_+=χ_- dot R_- "reduces" to dot R_h(t2)=0.
  • Exact proved inputs: III-E p3e:sec:v194-amplitude-flux-sync, lines 5105–5115, says χ is continuous positive and flux means continuity of normal derivative; explicitly denies zero-derivative implication. III-F p3f:thm:v266-gp-exact-k16-junction-condition, lines 9383–9414, proves χ+=χ->0 and allows transverse C¹ crossing. VI-A p8:thm:v2111-cyclic-k16-finite-arrival, lines 15502–15517 and 15540–15553, exhibits the actual admitted cyclic branch with dot R<0 at the K16 hit.
  • Missing/false inference: χ_+v_+=χ_-v_- and v_+=v_- cannot imply v_+=v_-=0 when χ_+=χ_->0; any common nonzero rate satisfies the equation. Under VI-A's certified cyclic branch, the rate is actually negative, so the false subclaim conflicts with upstream physical branch, not only an ambient toy example.
  • Positive control: v_+=v_-=0 satisfies the same matching law, demonstrating zero rate is a permitted special case, not a necessary condition.
  • Impact: the second boxed equation in the VI-B corollary is invalid. The no-free-time-width statement, transverse crossing law, K16 state/history and scalaron history are not thereby invalidated. No numerical/observable downstream route has yet been proved to consume the false zero-velocity clause. Later batches will map any actual uses.
  • Condition origin: upstream III-F smooth-Hessian and positive χ are existing derived conditions; no new occurrence or surface layer assumed.
  • Needed action: correct source inference in a separate paper-repair task (prohibited in this audit); in the DAG mark this subclaim inconsistent while preserving other clause statuses and evidence.
